title: Make room for the Name by wanting less
summary: The body can name a hundred pleasures, but Naam needs room in the heart. Let one desired thing remain unchosen so remembrance has somewhere to dwell.
takeaway: Make one deliberate space where Naam can dwell.
lifeApplication: Before buying, eating, or reaching for another comfort, pause and leave one appetite unanswered as an offering of room for the Name.

source.shortMeaning: The body has many pleasures, but Naam asks for an uncluttered dwelling in the heart.
source.lifeApplication: Choose one concrete restraint today so the Name is not crowded out by every bodily want.

evidence.coreClaim: The body has many pleasures, but Naam asks for an uncluttered dwelling in the heart.
evidence.turn: The shabad does not shame the body; it asks whether its pleasures have filled the chamber where Naam should live.
evidence.practicalImplication: Before buying, eating, or reaching for another comfort, pause and leave one appetite unanswered as an offering of room for the Name.
